# Engineering Readiness Checklist: Completion Column & Automatic Board Sweep

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements and design artifacts are complete, unambiguous, consistent and verifiable enough to implement from — before any code is written
**Created**: 2026-08-15
**Resolved**: 2026-08-16
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

**How to read this**: every item interrogates what is *written* in `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/` and `quickstart.md`. None of them asks whether code works — that is what the test suites in `quickstart.md` are for. An item fails when the requirement is missing, vague, contradictory or unmeasurable.

**Status**: all 53 items resolved. 40 were already satisfied by the artifacts as written; 13 exposed real defects that were repaired in the owning artifact before being checked. Every repair is listed in §Resolution log at the end, with the artifact it changed. No item was checked without evidence, and no product decision was invented — see the log for why each repair was derivable rather than chosen.

## Requirement Clarity & Measurability

- [x] CHK009 Is "currently on the board" defined precisely enough that a reader can evaluate the sweep condition without reading code? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
  - Yes. Spec §Key Entities defines a Ticket as either on the board (and in which column) or completed and off the board; FR-010 states completed tickets do not count; data-model §The central invariant gives the two-row predicate table. A reader can evaluate FR-009 from the spec alone.
- [x] CHK010 Is the reserved completed-status marker specified as an exact literal, and is its collision with a user-chosen column name of the same text explicitly addressed rather than ignored? [Ambiguity, Research R6, Contracts §5]
  - Yes. R6 fixes the literal `Completed` and addresses the collision head-on: the fields are display-only, nothing branches on them, and the authoritative record is the audit entry. Contracts §5 makes the machine-readable `completed` boolean the thing consumers must branch on, so the collision is cosmetic by construction rather than by luck.
- [x] CHK011 Is "at least one such ticket exists" phrased so that the empty-board case is unambiguously excluded? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
  - Yes. FR-009 carries the clause explicitly, US2 acceptance scenario 5 covers the empty board, and the first Edge Case states a project with nothing on the board is never swept.
- [x] CHK012 Is "completed ranks strictly after every column" expressed as a rule a reviewer can apply to any case, rather than as a hint about one function? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011a]
  - Yes. FR-011a states it as a general ordering rule; §Key Entities restates it for *any* ordering comparison between tickets; data-model §Ordering semantics works it through three concrete situations. It is not scoped to `validateParentMove`.
- [x] CHK013 Can the 5-second bound for open boards reflecting a sweep be measured against something stated, given the live-update debounce is specified in the design rather than the spec? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005, Research R7]
  - Yes. R7 states the existing channel's 200 ms debounce and one event per sweep; plan §Performance Goals states that this meets SC-005's 5 s bound with three orders of magnitude of margin. The measurement is stated in the artifacts, not left to the reader.
- [x] CHK014 Is SC-010 ("manual clearing drops to zero") measurable with an instrument this system actually has, or is it an aspiration stated as a criterion? [Measurability, Spec §SC-010]
  - Resolved by reclassification, not by checking it off. It was an aspiration stated as a gate: it measures operator behavior over time, so no artifact and no pre-merge test can satisfy or falsify it. SC-010 is now explicitly labelled a **post-launch adoption outcome that must not block implementation**, names its instrument (the existing audit log's `ticket.moved` / `ticket.deleted` entries), and the §Success Criteria preamble states that only pre-release criteria gate. The product intent is unchanged.
- [x] CHK015 Are the success criteria that claim "100% of cases" tied to a defined population of cases, so they can be falsified? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, §SC-003, §SC-007]
  - Yes. SC-002's population is "cases where the last ticket on the board enters the completion column of a project that has one"; SC-003's is "sweeps"; SC-007's is "swept tickets". Each is a countable set a test can enumerate.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK016 Do the move-triggered evaluation point and the state-based sweep condition read consistently, without implying that deletions or column-deletion relocations also trigger? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009]
  - Yes. FR-008 fixes the evaluation point (immediately after a move into the completion column) and FR-009 fixes the condition (a state). The two Edge Cases about deletion and column-deletion relocation state that those events do not trigger despite satisfying the state.
- [x] CHK017 Is the Assumptions entry recording the narrow trigger consistent with the two Edge Cases that describe events which deliberately do not trigger? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions, §Edge Cases]
  - Yes. The Assumptions entry names both events by the same description used in the Edge Cases and gives the same reason (under-trigger rather than surprise). The assumption now also names FR-008 and those Edge Cases as what would change if it were overturned.
- [x] CHK018 Do the board-excludes-completed requirement and the contract's deliberately unchanged endpoint default conflict, or is the reconciliation stated explicitly? [Conflict, Spec §FR-019a, Contracts §3, Research R4]
  - No conflict, and the reconciliation is explicit. R4 states that FR-019a is a requirement about the *board*, not the endpoint, and that the board satisfies it by passing `placement=board`; contracts §3 repeats it at the endpoint. T047 implements the board side, T040 asserts both halves.
- [x] CHK019 Is one canonical term used throughout for the designated column, with "terminal column" and "done column" either eliminated or explicitly noted as synonyms? [Consistency, Spec §Input vs §Requirements]
  - Yes, after repair. "Completion column" was already canonical in every requirement, but "terminal" survived in the feature slug and in one Dependencies line, with nothing saying they were the same thing. A new spec §Terminology declares the canonical term, records "terminal column" as a slug-only synonym, and separates both from `Done`, which is merely a default column *name*. The stray Dependencies line now says "completion column".
- [x] CHK020 Do the application-level clearing of a previous designation and the database-level uniqueness guarantee describe complementary mechanisms rather than the same one twice? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, Research R2]
  - Complementary, and R2 says so in as many words: the transactional clear-then-set is *the mechanism*, the partial unique index is *the guarantee*. R2 also explains the READ COMMITTED race that makes the second necessary rather than redundant.

## Contract & Compatibility Requirements

- [x] CHK021 Are requirements stated for every existing response field whose *type* changes, in particular a ticket's column identifier becoming nullable for consumers that assumed it never was? [Completeness, Contracts §3, §4]

The contracts preamble states the widening once and blanket-scopes it to *every ticket-bearing response*, including endpoints otherwise unchanged; §3 and §4 show it concretely; plan §Summary flags it as the feature's single compatibility change; data-model §Consumers enumerates every file that must handle it.
- [x] CHK022 Is "no MCP tool is renamed or removed" stated as an explicit requirement rather than left implicit? [Clarity, Contracts mcp-tools §Governing constraint]
  - Yes, in bold at the top of contracts/mcp-tools.md, with the constitutional reason (tool names are referenced as literal text, so renaming is a breaking change). T061 verifies it.
- [x] CHK023 Are requirements defined for how a caller distinguishes a successful sweep-triggering move from a failure, given the returned ticket has no column? [Clarity, Contracts §4, Research R5]
  - Yes. Contracts §4 specifies the additive `sweep` summary as the positive signal, states in a callout that `columnId: null` alongside a non-null `sweep` is the intended outcome and not an error, and preserves every existing error code so failures remain distinguishable. R5 gives the reasoning and now names the requirements it serves.
- [x] CHK024 Is the unchanged default of the ticket-listing endpoint and its MCP tool stated as a binding requirement, not merely as a design note? [Consistency, Contracts §3, mcp-tools §2]
  - Yes, and it is defended by tests rather than by assertion. Both contracts state the unchanged default in bold; T040 asserts that omitting `placement` returns everything exactly as before, and T049 asserts the MCP tool sends no `placement` when not given.
- [x] CHK025 Is the error condition for a rejected concurrent designation specified with a code and a required caller behavior? [Completeness, Contracts §2]
  - Yes: `409 COMPLETION_COLUMN_CONFLICT`, raised when the partial unique index rejects a concurrent double designation, with the losing caller required to retry. T022 maps the Prisma error rather than letting it surface raw.
- [x] CHK026 Are requirements stated confirming that no published port, endpoint path or ticket-project file shape is affected, so the breaking-change review is knowably not triggered? [Coverage, Plan §Constitution Check]
  - Yes. Plan's Technology Stack row states ports `:4000`, `:3000`, `127.0.0.1:5000`, `:5434`, every endpoint path, every MCP tool name and the `.claude/ticket-project.json` shape are unaffected, and identifies the `columnId` widening as the one compatibility change, which is a widening rather than a removal. T061 verifies it.

## Data Integrity & Migration Requirements

- [x] CHK027 Is the central invariant ("no column means exactly, and only, completed") stated as a requirement, with every writer that must uphold it enumerated? [Completeness, Data-model §The central invariant]
  - Yes. Data-model states the invariant as a blockquote and enumerates all three writers — `createTicket` always resolves a column, `updateTicket` rejects `columnId` outright, `moveTicket` is the only writer and the sweep the only nulling path — and requires a test (T014) that fails if a future change breaks it.
- [x] CHK028 Are requirements defined for what must happen if a ticket ever ends up with no column by any path other than a sweep? [Gap, Edge Case]
  - Yes, after repair. The artifacts previously defined only *prevention*. Data-model now specifies the required behavior on breach: **uniform treatment** — such a ticket is treated as completed by every consumer with no special-casing, no inference of a "real" column and no error path — which follows from the invariant's own definition rather than adding a new rule, and bounds the cost of a breach to "appears finished when it should not" instead of a crash or an invisible ticket.
- [x] CHK029 Is the decision to require no data backfill justified against the requirement that existing projects behave unchanged, in a way a reviewer can check? [Traceability, Data-model §Migration, Spec §FR-007]
  - Yes. Data-model §Migration ties it to FR-007 step by step: the `DEFAULT false` gives every existing column `false`, so no existing project has a completion column and none can be swept until opt-in, and every existing ticket keeps a non-null `columnId` and stays on the board. T007 is the explicit confirmation step.
- [x] CHK030 Are the migration's irreversibility conditions required to appear in the migration artifact itself, rather than only in the design documents? [Completeness, Data-model §Migration]
  - Yes, in three places that all point at the file: data-model ("noted in the migration file itself rather than discovered in production"), plan risk 2 ("Must be stated in the migration file itself, not just in the docs", now with an acceptance criterion), and T006, which requires the comment as part of writing the migration.
- [x] CHK031 Are requirements defined for detecting the silent loss of the partial unique index, given the schema language cannot express it? [Gap, Research R2]
  - Yes. R2's mitigation (b) requires a concurrency test that fails loudly if the guard disappears; T018 is that test and is labelled the tripwire; plan risk 1 now names T018 as its owner and "detected by CI rather than by a corrupted board" as its acceptance criterion. Mitigations (a) and (c) — the hand-written-migration convention and the schema comment (T004) — reduce the chance of the loss itself.
- [x] CHK032 Is the required ordering of migration statements specified wherever order actually matters? [Clarity, Data-model §Migration]
  - Yes. Data-model lists the three statements "in order" and T006 repeats "in this order". Order is load-bearing exactly once — the partial unique index cannot be created before the column it filters on exists — and both artifacts place it third.

## Failure Mode & Concurrency Requirements

- [x] CHK033 Are all three concurrency hazards — half-sweep, double-sweep and missed sweep — named separately, each with its own required behavior? [Completeness, Research R3]
  - Yes, in R3's hazard table: half-sweep (same transaction plus a single conditional `UPDATE`), double-sweep (second finds nothing, so audit and event fire only when rows were actually swept) and missed sweep (requires serialization, not a conditional statement). A fourth hazard, sweep-vs-delete, was added during this review — see CHK039.
- [x] CHK034 Is the missed-sweep hazard stated in observable terms a test can assert, rather than only as an isolation-level explanation? [Measurability, Research R3, Spec §SC-002]
  - Yes. R3 gives the observable symptom ("the board simply sits there full of Done cards") alongside the isolation-level cause, ties it to SC-002's 100% population, and T028 turns it into an assertion: concurrent moves into the completion column must produce exactly one sweep and never zero.
- [x] CHK035 Is the scope and duration of the serialization requirement bounded in writing, so it cannot be read as serializing unrelated projects? [Clarity, Research R3]
  - Yes, and the bound is now explicit on all three axes: scope is one project row (`WHERE id = $1`), duration is one move transaction with no external I/O and no user think-time, and the lock is taken only when the project has a completion column *and* the move targets it. T036 restates the condition so the narrow trigger survives into implementation.
- [x] CHK036 Are rollback requirements defined for a sweep that fails part-way, explicitly including the move that triggered it? [Coverage, Spec §FR-014]
  - Yes. FR-014 requires failure to leave the board "exactly as it was **before the triggering move**" and to be reported; contracts §4 states that a failing sweep rolls the move back; T027 asserts the triggering move is rolled back too, not just the sweep.
- [x] CHK037 Is it required that a sweep affecting zero tickets produces no audit entry and no live-update event? [Gap, Research R3, R7]
  - Yes. R3's double-sweep row requires the audit and event to be emitted "only when rows were actually swept", and T034 carries the condition into the audit task. The event follows the same publish-after-commit path and fires per sweep, not per attempt.
- [x] CHK038 Are requirements defined for a move that restores a completed ticket directly into the completion column, which would immediately re-satisfy the sweep condition? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-023]
  - Yes, after repair. The previous state was circular: T052 demanded behavior that was "documented rather than accidental" while no artifact documented it. A new spec Edge Case now states the outcome — this is a move into the completion column, so FR-008 requires evaluation and FR-017 forbids opting out; if it is the only board ticket it is swept again immediately, and restoring into any other column leaves it on the board. The outcome was *derived* from FR-008/FR-009/FR-017, not chosen. T052 now asserts that specific outcome.
- [x] CHK039 Are requirements defined for the interaction between a sweep and a concurrent deletion of one of the tickets being swept? [Gap, Coverage]
  - Yes, after repair. This was entirely unaddressed. `deleteTicket` runs in its own transaction and takes no project lock (`backend/src/services/tickets.ts`), so the interleave is real. R3 gains a fourth hazard row and a full paragraph: both orders are safe for the board — a ticket deleted first is not swept, a ticket swept first still deletes cleanly — and the actual risk is a **record that disagrees with reality**, so FR-021a now requires the audit's count and ids to come from the rows the `UPDATE` affected rather than from the earlier condition query. T034 carries the constraint; new T029b asserts both orders.

## Verification & Test Coverage Requirements

- [x] CHK040 Does every behavior-changing requirement map to at least one named test file, so Principle II's "every behavior change ships with tests" is checkable rather than asserted? [Traceability, Quickstart §What the new tests must demonstrate]
  - Yes, after repair. tasks.md declares the quickstart coverage table authoritative, but that table had **no rows** for audit and status history (FR-020, FR-021), for restore (FR-023, FR-024) or for creation being unaffected (FR-025) — all three were covered in tasks.md only, so the authoritative mapping contradicted the task list. The three rows were added, and the atomicity and MCP rows extended for FR-014a, FR-021a and passthrough fidelity. Every behavior-changing FR now names a file in the authoritative table.
- [x] CHK041 Are regression-test requirements stated for the surfaces claimed to be unchanged — reports, metrics and endpoint defaults? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019b, Contracts §6]
  - Yes, and they are required rather than assumed. Contracts §6 states the unchanged numbers are "a contract that must be defended by a regression test, not merely observed"; T041 and T042 assert report and metric figures across a sweep; T040 and T049 assert the endpoint and MCP defaults. T045 records the by-inspection confirmation that `reports.ts` and `metrics.ts` need no change, defended by T041/T042.
- [x] CHK042 Is "no sweep logic exists in the MCP layer" expressed as something a test can actually assert? [Measurability, Contracts mcp-tools §Tests]
  - Yes, after repair. As written it was unfalsifiable — the contract explicitly declined to test it, so a rule leaking in later would break nothing. It is now restated positively as **passthrough fidelity**, which is directly assertable: response fidelity (a stubbed sweep-bearing response is relayed unchanged, with no branching on `sweep` and no treating a null `columnId` as an error), request fidelity (exactly one `PATCH` with exactly `{ isCompletionColumn }`; `placement` forwarded verbatim or omitted entirely) and error fidelity (a `409` surfaces uninterpreted). New T049a owns these tests.
- [x] CHK043 Are test requirements defined for the invariant that ordinary create and update paths can never leave a ticket without a column? [Coverage, Data-model §The central invariant]
  - Yes. Data-model requires the test, the quickstart table carries an Invariant row, and T014 asserts that `createTicket` always assigns a column and `updateTicket` still rejects `columnId` with `400 VALIDATION`.
- [x] CHK044 Is the plugin suite's mandatory glob invocation form restated for this feature's gate, given the directory form fails on Windows? [Consistency, Constitution Principle II, Quickstart §Automated verification]
  - Yes. Quickstart §Automated verification shows `node --test plugin/tests/*.test.mjs` and states the glob form is mandatory; T002 restates it with the `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`-on-Windows warning; T064 runs "the exact commands in T002". `plugin/` is untouched, so the suite runs to prove exactly that.

## Dependencies, Assumptions & Carried Risk

- [x] CHK050 Is each Assumptions entry paired with the requirement it would change if overturned, so the cost of a wrong default is visible? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
  - Yes, after repair. The entries gave rationale but named no consequence. Each now carries an *If overturned* clause naming the affected requirements — single designation → FR-002/FR-009 plus the database guarantee; opt-in → FR-007/FR-012 plus a forbidden backfill; narrow trigger → FR-008 plus two inverted Edge Cases; off-the-board-as-state → FR-013/FR-019a and the whole data model; completed marker → FR-019; no confirmation → FR-013/FR-017 plus an undefined agent prompt; subtickets → FR-011/FR-011a; credited actor → FR-021/FR-021a plus a system identity that does not exist.
- [x] CHK051 Is the assumption that move operations are infrequent — the justification for the serialization approach — validated against something, or merely asserted? [Assumption, Research R3]
  - Validated, after repair. It was a bare assertion ("human- or agent-paced"). R3 now grounds it in three checkable facts about this repository: every write route in `backend/src/routes/` acts on a single entity and there is **no bulk or batch move path**, so arrival rate is bounded by discrete interactive actions; the lock's scope is one project row and its duration one short transaction with no external I/O; and the only contending case is two actors completing the same project at once, which is the case the lock exists for. R3 also records that adding a bulk-move capability expires this justification and forces re-evaluation.
- [x] CHK052 Do the two risks carried out of the design review have stated acceptance criteria or owners, rather than being logged and forgotten? [Gap, Plan §Constitution Check]
  - Yes, after repair. Both risks were logged with mitigations but no owner and no closure condition. Risk 1 (partial index invisible to Prisma) now names T004 and T018 as owners and is accepted when the tripwire test is in the suite that gates every PR. Risk 2 (migration not safely reversible) names T006 and is accepted only when the warning is in the migration file itself, with documentation elsewhere explicitly not discharging it.
- [x] CHK053 Are the explicitly out-of-scope items (bulk re-open, per-role restrictions, scheduled sweeping, backlog retention) stated as exclusions rather than omissions, so a reviewer can tell the difference? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]
  - Yes. Spec §Assumptions closes with a "**Scope excludes**" entry naming all four and recording that none was requested — an explicit exclusion with a reason, not a silent omission.
